correctness.rationale: Exact reflection-even/odd sector block diagonalization gives irreducible tridiagonal even block and a symmetric path odd block. The Chebyshev determinant recurrence proves (z²+γ²−4)U_{m−1}(z/2)² for all m≥2. Every even-block eigenspace is one-dimensional; comparison of simple Chebyshev zeros with the moving quadratic gives all Jordan sizes, boundaries and exceptional strengths. Nilpotent expansions yield matching upper and lower operator-norm growth laws. 23 finite symbolic/numeric checks corroborate selected instances, not the universal quantifier. No unverified infinite computation is used.

originality.rationale: Against inspected primary texts, the scope-limited result resolves exact Jordan sizes at every special gamma for every even ring and deduces distinct polynomial norm-growth regimes. Scott–Joglekar 2012 contains the geometry, Jin–Song 2016 contains the characteristic spectrum and four-site J3, Ortega–Benet–Larralde 2021 contains singular levels and six-site eta=2; these parts are excluded from novelty. None of the inspected relevant sections states the complete size-uniform embedded-Jordan/dynamical classification. This is a provisional same mathematical model historical assessment, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: The collision locations are immediate from the spectrum published in 2016; geometric-multiplicity and growth analysis may have appeared in less easily retrievable PT optical-ring literature or follow from broader general theorems.
The 2021 general eigenvector formulas could yield the stated multiplicities by a nontrivial specialization, even though this explicit classification was not located in the inspected sections.
Full historical priority and third-party verification remain unestablished.

value.rationale: The natural physical problem is whether a completely real non-Hermitian spectrum guarantees bounded optical/quantum coupled-mode amplification. The theorem identifies discrete subthreshold parameter values where it does not, a complete finite-size classification of every Jordan defect, and a parity-sharp linear-versus-quadratic amplification boundary. Spectral crossings alone do not answer the dynamic norm question. This directly informs interpretation of PT-symmetric gain/loss ring experiments and algebraic spectral stability.
